A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Splatent and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and references. However, neither includes the repeatedly cited Appendix, limiting comparison of appendix-only experiments and details.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on DL3DV-10K, LLFF, and Mip-NeRF360, reference-view ablations, and MVSplat360 integration results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports MEt3R multi-view consistency results in Table 2.

M1.justification: The documented latent 3DGS reconstruction, frozen VAE, reference-view grid, single-step diffusion refinement, training losses, and MVSplat360 integration remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use DL3DV-10K, LLFF, and Mip-NeRF360 with the same dense, sparse, and feed-forward scenarios. The added MEt3R evaluation uses existing DL3DV-10K coverage.

E2.justification: The displayed comparisons retain Feature-3DGS, LRF, and MVSplat360 in their corresponding settings. v2 newly mentions additional diffusion-based comparisons in the unavailable Appendix, so their comparator membership cannot be verified.

E3.justification: v2 adds MEt3R as an evaluation metric for dense and sparse DL3DV-10K reconstruction. Existing image-quality metrics, input-view counts, camera sampling, image resolution, and stated training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The reference-view ablation is unchanged from v1 Table 2 to v2 Table 3, as is Figure 3's spectral analysis. Appendix-only ablations cannot be compared, and v2's newly mentioned runtime and memory analysis is unavailable.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seed values, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new MEt3R table also reports point estimates without statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 Table 2 adds MEt3R scores: dense Feature-3DGS/LRF/Splatent results are 0.1106/0.1082/0.0774, and sparse results are 0.1281/0.1272/0.0998. These are newly reported results, not improvements over v1 scores. Existing benchmark, ablation, feed-forward, and qualitative results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(7), the latent-grid formulation, and mathematical definitions remain unchanged. MEt3R is introduced through a citation without a new mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims about latent reconstruction, reference-guided detail recovery, and feed-forward integration. The new consistency results support existing claims; removing the generic final sentence does not materially change their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly explains the MEt3R advantage through geometrically consistent low-frequency structure from 3D rendering, leaving diffusion to recover high-frequency details across views. The limitations in Section 6 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 newly specifies that the existing 400-scene training subset was randomly selected, without establishing a changed selection procedure. Hardware, training time, optimizer, and hyperparameters remain unchanged. Newly referenced appendix runtime and memory details cannot be verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds the MEt3R citation supporting its new evaluation. Research positioning otherwise remains stable. Duplicate Mip-NeRF360 and latent-diffusion references are consolidated, while other bibliographic revisions largely describe the same works.

P1.justification: v2 merges some introductory paragraphs, shortens several passages and the conclusion, corrects 'Gaussian platting,' and revises bibliography formatting and metadata. The overall section order and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the consistency table, moves the unchanged ablation table from page 7 to page 8, and renumbers the ablation and feed-forward tables. Several figures are resized and surrounding text reflows; Figures 1-5 retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The new MEt3R evaluation provides direct quantitative support for multi-view consistency, a central claim without a dedicated metric in v1. This and the small training-detail clarification improve the supplied paper modestly while preserving prior results. Unavailable appendix comparisons and runtime/memory analyses cannot be credited.
